explain.title: How does it work?
explain.whatText: It filters incoming connections — both the device's own services and the ports published by containers (Modbus, IEC 104, NATS…). While on, the first matching rule applies; connections matching no rule are blocked.
explain.guardText: The web interface and SSH (TCP {{ports}}) plus the remote maintenance tunnel are kept open on the device itself; no rule can close them. In an emergency, 'sudo e1-fwd.py disable' on the device console turns the firewall off.
explain.telemetryText: Remote gateways push telemetry over NATS (4222/TCP). If you enable the firewall without allowing this port, field data stops; the 'Service presets' buttons add the right ports with one click.

diag.ok: Flow is healthy: telemetry is being written to registers and SCADA is polling. If values still look empty, check the client-side address/format settings (FC3/FC4, unit ID, 40001 base offset, int16 vs float32).
diag.workerDown: The modbus-outbound service is unreachable — the container is down or its health port is closed.
diag.serverDown: Worker is up but no TCP server runs for this target — the target may be inactive or the plan failed to load (see plan sync error).
diag.consumerError: The telemetry consumer is failing — NATS connection/subscription problem:
diag.noTelemetry: No telemetry has been processed from NATS. Check that devices are sending data (Live Values updating) and the gateway/NATS are up; if the service just started it may be waiting for the first measurement (only new messages are processed, history is not replayed).
diag.unmapped: Telemetry arrives but does not match the device/signal keys in this target's address plan — the plan may be stale (refreshes every 30 s) or device codes differ.
diag.uncoercible: Telemetry arrives and matches the plan, but the value can't be coerced to a number/bit — the signal's numeric field may be empty (see the uncoercible counter).
diag.noWrites: Telemetry is processed but nothing was written to this target yet — the incoming signals may be outside the plan, or no measurement has arrived yet for this target's signals.
diag.noReads: Values are written to registers but SCADA has not read anything yet — the client connects but sends no queries, or is polling the wrong port.
diag.snapshotOnly: Live telemetry has never written to this target; registers are fed from last known values. SCADA reads data, but values only update on refresh cycles — check the device/gateway flow.
diag.snapshotDisabled: Nothing has been written to the registers and last-known-value refresh is OFF (MODBUS_SNAPSHOT_REFRESH_SEC=0). Signals that never change will read 0 in SCADA forever; enable the refresh.
